ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Ernest Hemingway Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care: heavy drinking, low mood and forgetfulness a year after two plane crashes, with high blood pressure and abnormal liver and iron tests on the intake panel. Concerns: He is afraid of losing his memory and his ability to write; He wants to drink less without being told he must never drink again; He worries about headaches and pain since the crashes. [S]

tr.td: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram at the diagnosis of hypertension: sinus rhythm at 86, normal intervals, borderline voltage for left ventricular hypertrophy
Transient elastography of the liver in the hepatology clinic: liver stiffness 9.4 kPa (indeterminate); controlled attenuation parameter 288 dB/m (fatty change)

MRI of the liver without contrast with R2* liver iron quantification and magnetic resonance elastography: liver iron concentration about 9.8 mg Fe/g dry weight (raised); stiffness 3.1 kPa, in keeping with mild fibrosis and no advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis; no liver lesion

Transthoracic echocardiogram for stage 2 hypertension and iron overload: mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, ejection fraction 60%, normal diastolic filling for age, no features of iron-related cardiomyopathy
Therapeutic phlebotomy, 500 mL weekly at the clinic's infusion room, with a hemoglobin check before each session (held if under 12.0 g/dL); twenty-two sessions before the six-month visit
Advance care planning conversation, about 18 minutes
Tdap vaccine for a tetanus-prone wound; last tetanus booster more than ten years ago
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20), one dose for chronic liver disease and alcohol use disorder
Hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccine, dose 1 of 3, for chronic liver disease after nonreactive hepatitis B tests

tr.td: Establishing primary care: heavy drinking, low mood and forgetfulness a year after two plane crashes, with high blood pressure and abnormal liver and iron tests on the intake panel
Two-week review with the hepatology consultation: HFE result, liver stiffness and the phlebotomy plan
Six-week review: phlebotomy, drinking, mood, blood pressure and liver imaging
Fourteen-week review: phlebotomy, the decision to stop drinking, mood and blood pressure
Six-month review: iron, liver, mood, memory and the plan for maintenance phlebotomy
Same-day sick visit for a fishhook wound of the hand with early cellulitis

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Alcohol: AUDIT and DSM-5-TR assessment, brief intervention in his own terms, naltrexone 50 mg daily, thiamine, a drinking diary, a goal he chooses and revisits, withdrawal precautions if he stops (no abrupt stop at his intake level without a plan), and mutual-help or counseling options offered
Hepatology consultation for raised iron studies and liver tests in a heavy drinker: to confirm the cause, stage the liver, and plan treatment

Hemochromatosis: weekly phlebotomy of 500 mL with a hemoglobin check before each, to a ferritin of 50 to 100 ng/mL, then maintenance; MRI with liver iron quantification and elastography instead of biopsy; no iron or vitamin C supplements, no raw shellfish; no alcohol advised while iron is high and the liver is healing; HFE and iron testing offered to first-degree relatives through a letter he may share, with no result recorded here

Depression: PHQ-9 at each visit, weekly psychotherapy (cognitive behavioral therapy) with the clinic's behavioral health clinician, sertraline, the Mood Disorder Questionnaire before the antidepressant, a structured safety assessment with a written safety plan, lethal-means counseling about firearms, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit

Post-concussion symptoms: symptom-based care (headache plan without daily analgesics, sleep routine, graded activity, writing in shorter sessions), MoCA repeated after three months with less alcohol, no routine brain imaging without warning signs, and neuropsychological testing if thinking does not improve; chronic traumatic encephalopathy not diagnosed
Hypertension: home blood pressure monitoring, amlodipine, less alcohol and salt, ECG and urine albumin at diagnosis, echocardiogram for stage 2 hypertension, and a target below 130/80 mmHg
Prediabetes: HbA1c repeated at six months, less alcohol, activity and diet; iron overload and alcohol both raise the risk of diabetes
Drinking goal chosen by him: no more than two drinks a day and none before evening, then reconsidered once the liver results are known
Reduced to three or four drinks a day by six weeks; he then chose to stop, and has had no alcohol for three weeks
Ferritin 50 to 100 ng/mL with weekly phlebotomy, then maintenance
Ferritin 1,460 to 268 ng/mL after twenty-two sessions; induction continuing
PHQ-9 16 to 5 at six months; response, nearly in remission
126/78 in clinic and an average of 124/76 at home on amlodipine 10 mg
Fewer headaches and clearer thinking, so that he can write
Headaches once a week from three; MoCA 25 to 27; writing every morning

Alert, courteous and guarded at first, then direct; speech normal in rate; smells of alcohol at a late-morning visit without signs of intoxication or withdrawal [S]

MoCA 25 of 30: lost points on delayed recall and serial sevens; oriented; language and visuospatial items normal [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1955-03-02: current ideation present, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with close follow-up. C-SSRS screen: wish to be dead on several days in the past month; no active thoughts of suicide, intent, plan, preparation or past attempt. Risk factors reviewed without detail: a father who died by suicide, other deaths by suicide in his family, heavy drinking, depression, repeated head injuries, chronic pain, and firearms at home. Lethal-means counseling about firearms was done respectfully, as a hunter's safety question rather than a judgment: he chose to have his guns held in the locked storage at his shooting club while his mood and drinking are treated, and to keep no ammunition at home. A written safety plan was made with him, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in his phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit [S]
